back: An Ndebele word for "the rising"; the Ndebele rebellion of 1896.
A deadly cattle disease that reached the country in 1896 and killed large numbers of herds.

front: When did the Ndebele rising begin, and when did the Shona rise?
back: Ndebele in March 1896; Shona in June 1896.

front: What effect did the Jameson Raid have on the risings?
back: It took many Company police out of the country and gave an opportunity.

front: Who were the main religious leaders in Mashonaland?
Which priest of the Mwari cult helped to spread the rising to Mashonaland?
Name five causes of the 1896 risings.
back: Loss of land, loss of cattle, forced labour, taxes and the Native Police, plus loss of independence and the disasters of 1895-96.

front: What did the Native Police do to cause resentment?
back: They collected taxes and enforced labour, and were accused of cruelty and cattle theft.

front: How did historians disagree about coordination?
back: Ranger saw linked religious leadership; Cobbing stressed local causes; many now accept some links but separate risings.
